title: Impact of Catalytic Converter Mandate on NOx Emissions

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (unit and period). The policy (catalytic converter mandate) applies to treated regions in the post period; untreated regions serve as controls.
- Why: We compare changes in log NOx emissions over time between treated and control regions, differencing out time-invariant unit heterogeneity and common shocks via period fixed effects.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the mandate, treated and control regions would have experienced the same trend in log NOx emissions.
  - No spillovers: The mandate in treated regions does not affect emissions in control regions.
  - Stable composition and SUTVA: Units and their measurement are stable across periods; treatment is well-defined.
  - Exogeneity of timing: No unobserved shocks coincident with treatment that differentially affect treated regions relative to controls.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Install/load required packages
req_pkgs <- c("data.table", "dplyr", "fixest", "sandwich", "lmtest")
new_pkgs <- req_pkgs[!(req_pkgs %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
if(length(new_pkgs)) install.packages(new_pkgs, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
invisible(lapply(req_pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE))

options(scipen = 999, digits = 4)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s47_data.csv"
df <- data.table::fread(path)
df <- as.data.frame(df)

# Basic checks and preparation
df$unit_id <- as.integer(df$unit_id)
df$period  <- as.integer(df$period)
df$treated <- as.integer(df$treated)
df$post    <- as.integer(df$post)
df$treat_x_post <- as.integer(df$treat_x_post)

cat("Data summary:\n")
cat("Units:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), 
    "| Periods:", length(unique(df$period)), 
    "| Obs:", nrow(df), "\n\n")

# Helper: function to print estimate summaries
print_est <- function(name, beta, se, dof = NULL){
  z <- beta / se
  # Use normal approx for p-value; with clustering, small #units may need t-dist, but z is fine for quick print.
  p <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z)))
  ci_low <- beta - 1.96 * se
  ci_high <- beta + 1.96 * se
  pct <- 100 * (exp(beta) - 1) # outcome is log, interpret as percent change
  pct_lo <- 100 * (exp(ci_low) - 1)
  pct_hi <- 100 * (exp(ci_high) - 1)
  cat(paste0(name, ":\n",
             "  DID coef (log points) = ", sprintf("%.4f", beta),
             " | SE = ", sprintf("%.4f", se),
             " | 95% CI = [", sprintf("%.4f", ci_low), ", ", sprintf("%.4f", ci_high), "]",
             " | p = ", sprintf("%.4f", p), "\n",
             "  Implied % change = ", sprintf("%.2f", pct), "% (95% CI: ",
             sprintf("%.2f", pct_lo), "%, ", sprintf("%.2f", pct_hi), "%)\n\n"))
}

# 2) Baseline DID via OLS with treated + post + interaction, cluster-robust SE by unit
did_ols <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
vc_ols  <- sandwich::vcovCL(did_ols, cluster = ~ unit_id, type = "HC1")
ct_ols  <- lmtest::coeftest(did_ols, vcov = vc_ols)
beta_ols <- unname(coef(did_ols)["treat_x_post"])
se_ols   <- sqrt(diag(vc_ols))["treat_x_post"]

cat("Baseline DID (OLS with main effects + interaction), clustered by unit:\n")
print_est("OLS-DID", beta_ols, se_ols)

# 3) Two-way fixed effects (unit and period) DID, clustered by unit
# Note: in TWFE, we include unit and period FEs; the DID effect is on treat_x_post
twfe <- fixest::feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)
beta_twfe <- unname(fixest::coef(twfe)["treat_x_post"])
se_twfe   <- sqrt(diag(fixest::vcov(twfe)))["treat_x_post"]

cat("Two-way Fixed Effects DID (unit and period FE), clustered by unit:\n")
print_est("TWFE-DID", beta_twfe, se_twfe)

# 4) Event-study style robustness (if >= 3 periods and both pre and post exist)
do_es <- (length(unique(df$period)) >= 3) && any(df$post == 0) && any(df$post == 1)
if (do_es) {
  base_pre <- max(df$period[df$post == 0], na.rm = TRUE)
  es_mod <- tryCatch({
    fixest::feols(y ~ i(period, treated, ref = base_pre) | unit_id + period, 
                  data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (!is.null(es_mod)) {
    cat("Event-study (i(period, treated, ref=last pre), with unit and period FE):\n")
    es_coef <- fixest::coef(es_mod)
    es_vcov <- fixest::vcov(es_mod)
    es_names <- names(es_coef)
    
    # Map coefficient names to period numbers (robust parsing)
    extract_period <- function(nm){
      # try to extract the first/last integer in the name
      digs <- gregexpr("[0-9]+", nm)
      ints <- regmatches(nm, digs)[[1]]
      if (length(ints) == 0) return(NA_integer_)
      # Take the last integer token as period label
      as.integer(tail(ints, 1))
    }
    period_map <- sapply(es_names, extract_period)
    
    # Identify pre-period interaction coefficients (period < base_pre)
    pre_idx <- which(!is.na(period_map) & (period_map < base_pre) & grepl("treated", es_names))
    post_idx <- which(!is.na(period_map) & (period_map > base_pre) & grepl("treated", es_names))
    
    # Joint test: all pre-period coefficients = 0 (pre-trend)
    pre_pval <- NA
    if (length(pre_idx) > 0) {
      # Use fixest::wald with the exact coefficient names
      wald_res <- tryCatch({
        hyp <- paste0(es_names[pre_idx], " = 0")
        fixest::wald(es_mod, hyp)
      }, error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!is.null(wald_res)) {
        pre_pval <- wald_res$p.value
      }
    }
    
    # Report max absolute pre-period deviation and joint p-value
    if (length(pre_idx) > 0) {
      pre_betas <- es_coef[pre_idx]
      cat(paste0("  Pre-trend check: max |pre-period beta| = ",
                 sprintf("%.4f", max(abs(pre_betas))),
                 ifelse(!is.na(pre_pval),
                        paste0(" | Joint pre-period H0 (all=0) p = ", sprintf("%.4f", pre_pval)),
                        " | Joint pre-period test not computed"),
                 "\n\n"))
    } else {
      cat("  Pre-trend check: insufficient pre-period variation to test.\n\n")
    }
  } else {
    cat("Event-study model could not be estimated.\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Event-study skipped (need >= 3 periods with both pre and post).\n\n")
}

# 5) Change-score DID (first-difference) as robustness
# Compute within-unit change from pre to post and regress on treated
df_pre <- df %>% dplyr::filter(post == 0) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(unit_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(y_pre = mean(y), treated = dplyr::first(treated), .groups = "drop")
df_post <- df %>% dplyr::filter(post == 1) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(unit_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(y_post = mean(y), .groups = "drop")
df_delta <- dplyr::inner_join(df_pre, df_post, by = "unit_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(delta = y_post - y_pre)

if (nrow(df_delta) >= 5 && length(unique(df_delta$treated)) == 2) {
  did_diff <- lm(delta ~ treated, data = df_delta)
  vc_diff  <- sandwich::vcovHC(did_diff, type = "HC1")
  beta_diff <- unname(coef(did_diff)["treated"])
  se_diff   <- sqrt(diag(vc_diff))["treated"]
  cat("Change-score DID (first-difference pre->post), robust SE:\n")
  print_est("FD-DID", beta_diff, se_diff)
} else {
  cat("Change-score DID skipped (insufficient matched pre/post per unit or no variation in treated).\n")
}

# Final concise summary of primary estimate (TWFE preferred)
cat("Primary estimate (TWFE-DID, log points): ", sprintf("%.4f", beta_twfe), "\n")
cat("Implied percent change in NOx: ", sprintf("%.2f", 100*(exp(beta_twfe)-1)), "%\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Catalytic converters reduce NOx emissions; thus the DID coefficient on treated × post (in logs) should be below zero.
- Magnitude: Common estimates suggest a sizable decline. For urban fleets with meaningful turnover and compliance, a 10–30% reduction is plausible over the post period. In log terms, this corresponds to roughly −0.10 to −0.35. The exact estimate depends on compliance rates, fleet age structure, and contemporaneous policies, but a central effect around −0.20 (≈18% reduction) is a reasonable expectation.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log NOx emissions between treated and untreated regions over time.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The catalytic converter mandate significantly reduces log NOx emissions.
